authority: SIRI – Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration
field_label: Fast-track scheme: employer pre-certification by SIRI
deadline_label: At least 4–6 weeks before first permit application
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers may sponsor non-EU work permits through the Fast-track scheme, which guarantees a SIRI decision within 10 business days of a complete application.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The Fast-track channel requires the employer to hold a valid SIRI certification obtained separately before any individual permit application. Most HR teams discover this only when the first permit is rejected for lack of certification, adding 2–4 weeks to the timeline.
non_obvious_action_required: Apply for Fast-track employer certification via nyidanmark.dk well before the first non-EU hire's arrival. SIRI assesses financial solvency and compliance history; certification must be periodically renewed. Do not assume certification is granted on first application.
source: SIRI – Fast-track scheme for certified employers

form_name: Residence and work permit application (online, nyidanmark.dk)
field_label: Work and residence permit – Pay Limit, Positive List, or Fast-track scheme
deadline_label: Submit at least 10–90 business days before start date (scheme-dependent)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals require a work and residence permit before beginning employment in Denmark. Three main routes: Pay Limit scheme (annual gross salary ≥ DKK 448,000, updated 1 January each year), Positive List scheme (shortage occupations listed by SIRI, updated twice yearly), and Fast-track scheme (certified employers, 10-business-day processing).
non_obvious_actual_reality: The Pay Limit salary threshold is recalculated each 1 January. A contract signed in December at a salary that met the old threshold may fall below the January figure, dropping the application into the Positive List track with 3–4 month processing. Salary in the permit application must match the contractual gross base; non-consolidated bonuses and benefits are excluded from the threshold calculation.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm the current year's Pay Limit threshold before contract signing. Lock base salary in the employment contract at or above the threshold with a buffer. If using Fast-track, confirm employer certification is active (step 1). Monitor threshold changes each January for existing permit holders approaching renewal.

authority: Home-country social security authority (e.g. CLEISS/URSSAF for France, NAV for Norway, SSA for USA)
form_name: A1 Certificate (EU/EEA posted workers) / Certificate of Coverage (bilateral agreement countries)
field_label: Social security coverage certificate – A1 or bilateral CoC
deadline_label: Obtain and deliver to HR before first working day in Denmark
non_obvious_official_guidance: Workers posted from EU/EEA countries remain in their home social security system under Regulation 883/2004 and must carry an A1 certificate. Denmark holds bilateral social security agreements with the USA, India, Canada, Australia, South Korea, Turkey, Pakistan, Morocco, Philippines, Serbia, and others.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without a valid A1 or bilateral Certificate of Coverage, full Danish social security contributions become mandatory: 8% AM-bidrag (employee) plus employer-side ATP and pension contributions. ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension) is a flat mandatory contribution for all Danish employees regardless of posted-worker status and is routinely omitted from employer cost models. Dual contributions in two countries simultaneously can arise for non-agreement nationals and are only resolved by advance planning.
non_obvious_action_required: Apply for the A1 or bilateral CoC before the employee's first working day. For permanently relocated employees, budget the full Danish social security stack. For senior employees, have a tax adviser assess PE (permanent establishment) risk if they retain significant decision-making authority over a foreign entity while based in Denmark.
source: Skattestyrelsen – Social security for internationally mobile employees

form_name: Folkeregister address registration (borger.dk online or in-person borgerservice)
deadline_label: Within 5 days of taking up residence – statutory deadline
non_obvious_official_guidance: All residents of Denmark must register their current address in the Civil Registration System (folkeregistret) within 5 days of moving in, whether in permanent or temporary accommodation.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The folkeregister address is the root anchor for CPR number, local tax municipality (kommunal skatteprocent varies 22–27% across municipalities), yellow health card catchment area, and GP registration eligibility. An incorrect or delayed folkeregister entry causes wrong local tax withholding and can restrict GP choice. If permanent housing is not yet secured, the employer's address may be used temporarily — but must be updated immediately on moving to permanent accommodation.
non_obvious_action_required: Register at borger.dk (requires existing MitID) or visit the local borgerservice in person. New arrivals without MitID must attend in person. Bring proof of tenancy (lease agreement or landlord letter) and valid ID. Update the record immediately on any address change — stale folkeregister addresses cascade into wrong tax municipality withholding.
source: Borger.dk – Register address when moving to Denmark

field_label: EU/EEA registration certificate and CPR number (ICS appointment)
deadline_label: Statutory deadline: 3 months after arrival — but ICS appointment wait is 4–8 weeks in Copenhagen; book on Day 1
non_obvious_official_guidance: EU/EEA nationals intending to stay and work in Denmark for more than 3 months must obtain an EU residence certificate (EU-registreringsbevis) from the local municipality or International Citizen Service.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The statutory 3-month window is misleading: ICS appointment availability in Copenhagen typically runs 4–8 weeks out. The EU certificate and CPR number are issued at the same ICS appointment — without this appointment, EU nationals have no CPR number, which blocks bank account opening, MitID activation, tax card registration, and NemKonto designation. An EU national without a CPR number is in digital limbo for everything.
non_obvious_action_required: Book an ICS appointment online immediately on arrival — or from the home country if the move date is known. Bring: valid EU passport or national ID, employment contract or employer letter, and proof of Danish address. ICS locations with English-language service: Copenhagen (Statsborgerservice), Aarhus, Odense, Aalborg. Accept any available appointment; do not defer while waiting for a preferred date.
source: Life in Denmark (borger.dk) – EU citizen registration

authority: Danish Civil Registration System (CPR) / Danish Immigration Service
form_name: CPR registration (automatic with residence permit; collect permit card at SIRI or by post)
deadline_label: CPR assigned at permit issuance; note number from decision letter and act within first week
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals receive a CPR number automatically when the Danish Immigration Service issues their residence permit. The CPR number appears in the permit decision letter.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Although CPR is assigned automatically, the physical residence permit card (opholdstilladelseskort) and CPR confirmation may take 1–2 weeks to arrive by post. The CPR number itself is in the decision letter and is fully functional immediately — banks, SKAT, and MitID issuers accept it without the physical card. Waiting for the card before acting causes cascading delays: no bank account, no tax card, no MitID, first payslip at 55% withholding rate.
non_obvious_action_required: Extract the CPR number from the residence permit decision letter on receipt. Use it immediately to open a bank account, initiate tax card registration, and book a MitID appointment. Register the folkeregister address (step 4) first — the CPR is anchored to the registered address. Do not wait for the physical card.
source: SIRI – CPR registration for non-EU permit holders

deadline_label: As soon as CPR is confirmed; before first payslip
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees should open a Danish bank account to receive salary and to designate a NemKonto for government disbursements.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Most major Danish banks (Danske Bank, Nordea, Sydbank, Jyske Bank) require a CPR number to open an account. This creates a bottleneck for EU nationals waiting for an ICS appointment and non-EU nationals whose CPR card is in the post. Some banks — notably Arbejdernes Landsbank and digital-first banks such as Lunar — can open accounts with a passport only, before CPR is confirmed. Without a Danish bank account, the employer cannot process salary to a NemKonto, potentially triggering default government payment routing.
non_obvious_action_required: Research the bank's CPR requirement before arrival. If CPR will be delayed, use Arbejdernes Landsbank or a digital bank as a bridge account immediately and migrate to a preferred bank once CPR is confirmed. Inform HR of the bank account IBAN and sort code as soon as the account is open to avoid payroll delays.
source: Life in Denmark (borger.dk) – Opening a bank account

form_name: MitID activation – online via mitid.dk or in-person at MitID issuer (bank branch or borgerservice)
deadline_label: Within 2–3 weeks of CPR; before any digital government service access
non_obvious_official_guidance: MitID is Denmark's national digital identity solution (replaced NemID in 2023), required to access SKAT TastSelv, borger.dk, e-boks (official digital post), and most online banking services.
non_obvious_actual_reality: MitID is not sent automatically — it must be actively initiated. Without MitID, the employee cannot view their tax card or årsopgørelse on skat.dk, cannot access official government digital post in e-boks (including CPR confirmation letters), cannot apply for the forsker tax scheme online, and cannot designate a NemKonto. New arrivals frequently spend 3–4 weeks in digital blackout because they do not realise MitID is a prerequisite for everything else. Some bank branches issue MitID at account opening — ask explicitly. Otherwise, book at a borgerservice office.
non_obvious_action_required: Book a MitID appointment at a participating bank branch or borgerservice office immediately after receiving the CPR number. Bring valid passport and CPR number. Install the MitID app on a smartphone before the appointment. MitID must be active before tax card registration (step 9), NemKonto designation (step 10), forsker scheme application (step 11), and GP registration (step 12).
source: MitID – Getting MitID as a newcomer to Denmark

form_name: Preliminary income assessment / tax card (forskudsopgørelse / skattekort) via TastSelv (skat.dk)
field_label: Tax card (skattekort) registration and SKAT onboarding
deadline_label: Before first payroll processing run — apply within days of MitID activation
non_obvious_official_guidance: New Danish tax residents must register with Skattestyrelsen and obtain a tax card (skattekort). The employer retrieves the card via eIndkomst and uses it to withhold the correct rate.
non_obvious_actual_reality: If no valid tax card is on file when payroll is processed, Danish law requires the employer to withhold at the maximum rate: 8% AM-bidrag plus 55% on income above the withholding-free amount (frikort threshold ~DKK 51,600/year in 2024). A missed tax card can result in the employee receiving less than 40% of gross salary in their first payslip — a cash-flow shock that is only corrected via the following year's årsopgørelse, not immediately. The tax card is also employer-specific (linked to CVR number); a role or employer change requires a new card.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must supply the company's CVR number to the employee on Day 1. Employee logs in to TastSelv at skat.dk (requires MitID), updates the preliminary income assessment with expected Danish salary and employment dates, and generates a tax card linked to the employer's CVR. Employer retrieves the card via eIndkomst before the first payroll run. Treat this as a payroll-blocking prerequisite.
source: Skattestyrelsen – Tax card for new employees

form_name: NemKonto bank account designation (borger.dk or nemkonto.dk, requires MitID)
field_label: NemKonto – official government payment account designation
deadline_label: Within 30 days of opening Danish bank account

form_name: Application for forsker- og nøglemedarbejderordningen (joint employer and employee application via TastSelv)
field_label: 27% flat-rate tax scheme for researchers and key employees (forskerordningen)
deadline_label: BEFORE first salary payment — cannot be applied retroactively under any circumstances
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees who have not been Danish tax residents in the 10 years before taking up Danish employment, and whose gross monthly salary meets the statutory minimum, may opt for a flat 27% income tax rate (plus 8% AM-bidrag, effective ~32.8%) for up to 84 months under the researcher and key employee scheme.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The forsker scheme is one of the most financially material and most routinely missed steps in Danish international onboarding. The 2024 minimum gross salary threshold is approximately DKK 75,600/month (updated annually 1 January). Over 84 months, a senior hire on DKK 1.2 M/year saves roughly DKK 400,000–600,000 versus standard Danish marginal tax (up to 56%). The scheme is permanently unavailable if the application is not approved before the payroll run covering the employee's first working day — missing the first payslip by a single cycle closes the window entirely for that employment. Most HR teams do not screen for this.
non_obvious_action_required: HR should screen every incoming non-Danish-resident hire against the salary threshold before contract signing. If eligible, both employer and employee must submit a joint application through SKAT TastSelv (requires MitID) before the payroll run that covers Day 1. Required documentation: signed employment contract, confirmation of non-Danish tax residency for the prior 10 years. Mark this as a Day 1 payroll-blocking priority alongside the tax card.

form_name: GP registration via sundhed.dk (requires MitID and CPR)
field_label: Yellow health card (sundhedskort) and GP (praktiserende læge) registration
deadline_label: Register with GP within first month; health card arrives by post 3–4 weeks after CPR
non_obvious_official_guidance: All Danish residents with a CPR number are entitled to a yellow health card (sundhedskort) and free access to the Danish public healthcare system, including GP, specialist referrals, hospital care, and subsidised prescriptions.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The yellow health card is mailed automatically to the folkeregister address 3–4 weeks after CPR registration, but GP registration is not automatic. Without an actively registered GP, the employee has no referral pathway to specialists and will be billed private rates for GP visits. GP catchment areas are fixed by geography — if the preferred practice is full, the system allocates the nearest available. Registration is via sundhed.dk using MitID; it can be completed before the physical card arrives.
non_obvious_action_required: Once MitID is active, go to sundhed.dk, search GPs within the catchment area of the registered folkeregister address, and complete registration with a practice. Do not wait for the physical health card. If the preferred GP has no capacity, register with any available practice in the area to avoid being unregistered — you can transfer to a preferred GP later when a slot opens.
source: Sundhed.dk – Find and register with a GP

form_name: Annual tax assessment review and amendment (årsopgørelse, via TastSelv at skat.dk)
field_label: Annual tax return review and deduction claims (årsopgørelse)
deadline_label: Available from March; review and amend by 1 May; corrections accepted until 1 August
non_obvious_official_guidance: Skattestyrelsen auto-generates a preliminary annual tax assessment (årsopgørelse) for all Danish tax residents each spring, pre-populated with data from employers, banks, and financial institutions.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Denmark's pre-filled return leads most employees to assume nothing needs to be done. However, several significant deductions are not pre-filled and must be claimed manually each year: commuting allowance (befordringsfradrag — DKK 0 for the first 24 km, capped annually for longer commutes; the most widely missed deduction), trade union membership fees (fagforeningskontingent), A-kasse (unemployment fund) contributions, and interest deductions on foreign-held loans. New residents on the forsker scheme have additional annual declarations. Missing the commuting deduction alone typically costs DKK 5,000–15,000 in unclaimed refunds per year.
non_obvious_action_required: Log in to TastSelv at skat.dk each March to review the pre-filled årsopgørelse before the 1 May deadline. Enter commuting data using the SKAT kilometre calculator (home address to workplace address, number of days worked per year). Add any A-kasse, union fee, and foreign loan interest figures. Approve or amend and submit. Tax refunds are processed within 2–4 weeks of submission.

deadline_label: Apply at least 2 months before current permit expiry date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Non-EU nationals must renew their Danish residence permit before the current permit expires to maintain lawful residence and right to work.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Denmark does not grant an automatic statutory grace period for expired permits. An employee whose permit lapses — even by one day — loses the legal right to work and may trigger immigration enforcement. Unlike some EU countries, there is no bridging right while a renewal application is pending unless the application was lodged before the expiry date. If the employee's salary, role, or employer has changed since the original permit was issued, a permit amendment rather than a standard renewal may be required — adding weeks to processing time. Permit expiry dates are not automatically tracked by SIRI or the employer.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must maintain a calendar of permit expiry dates for all non-EU employees and trigger renewal at least 2 months before the expiry date. Verify that salary still meets the applicable scheme threshold at the time of renewal. Any contract change (salary adjustment, job title change, employer change) should be assessed against permit conditions before it takes effect — undisclosed changes discovered at renewal can result in application refusal.

form_name: Social security classification review; A1 renewal (EU) or bilateral CoC renewal (non-EU); PE risk assessment
field_label: Annual social security and permanent establishment risk review
deadline_label: Annually or on any change in employment conditions or working pattern
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers of internationally mobile employees must confirm annually that each employee's social security coverage is correctly classified — either under a valid home-country A1/CoC or under full Danish mandatory contributions.
non_obvious_actual_reality: As posted workers transition from temporary assignments to permanent Danish-based roles, their posted-worker A1 coverage ceases to apply and full Danish social security (AM-bidrag, ATP, employer pension) becomes mandatory — a change that is often missed at the HR level. Additionally, senior employees who retain significant decision-making authority over a foreign parent or subsidiary while resident in Denmark may create a Permanent Establishment (PE) for the foreign entity under Danish corporate tax rules, exposing it to Danish corporate tax filing obligations. This is an invisible exposure that only surfaces in tax audits. A1 certificates extended beyond their original duration must be renewed formally; many lapse unnoticed.
non_obvious_action_required: Conduct an annual social security classification review for every internationally mobile employee. Flag any employee posted for more than 12 months for reclassification review. Engage a tax adviser for any C-level or senior manager working from Denmark who has authority over decisions of a foreign entity. Renew A1 certificates before lapse; do not assume auto-renewal.
source: Skattestyrelsen – Employers with internationally mobile employees
